Arrow wounds were particularly dangerous because the ligaments used to fasten the arrow-
head to the shaft became loosened when wetted with blood, so that if the shaft was pulled free the
arrowhead would easily dislodge. Having very rough edges (unlike bullets), all subsequent movement
caused friction with the arrowhead and rapid infection. Only by surgical removal of the whole arrow
could this be avoided.
